answer: Binding Deposit Against Flow History. Each agent identity posts a deposit locked to its cumulative transaction flow, and the cap rises as an ocean of prior counterparties co-signs activity, so a fresh clone starts at zero with no flow to draw on. A river of transfer history must accumulate before the cap unlocks, delaying any usable volume. An unused zephyr of activity earns no interest and expires, so the attacker pays full deposit plus foregone yield per clone while gaining almost no capacity, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
